title: Normalized closed support and strict-limit comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite-field datum $D$, and a specified unit $\ell\in D.k$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be complementary closed and quasi-compact open immersions over $D.k$, with $X$ separated finite type and $Z,U$ finite type. Use the specified completed coefficient operations of [def-sf-integral-support-normalization-data] and their residue-field inverses. There is an ordinary integral comparison for $i$ whose actual reduction square is invertible. Ordinary module direct image is exact. The inverse of $\mathrm{closedAlpha}$ gives $d_i$ from the actual strict-system direct image to ordinary direct image, with the stated projection formula and actual finite reduction maps invertible. Ordinary direct image preserves derived completeness and every common reduction interval. The actual restricted closed direct image has its specified shift, agrees with $d_i$ and the universal-unit termwise comparison, and is exact. Its composite with actual open pullback is zero. These are precisely $\mathrm{ClosedSupport}$; this statement does not assert any open-extension comparison, either restricted adjunction, or any unit/counit restriction formula.

source.place: Triangle, Hom vanishing and constructibility paragraphs; the detailed integral normalization argument is the seven-step proof of lem-sf-integral-support-functor-normalization, refined below.

proof.text: Obtain ordinary recollement R from sfIntegralOrdinaryRecollement_realization and take C=R.closed. Its ordinary right adjunction supplies finite limits; its kernel adjunction supplies finite colimits of completed module direct image. Install the normalized strict reduction-square isomorphism from lem-sf-closed-reduction-comparison.

On a constructible input the actual reconstruction unit is invertible by the specified coefficient system model. closedAlpha is ordinary image of this unit followed by the isomorphism closedLimit. Thus it is invertible objectwise and naturally. Define di as the inverse. The normalization theorem gives its inverse projection formula and the shift square of di by inverse compatibility.

The existing completed_image_complete proof transfers completeness along C.diagrams to ordinary completed direct image, for arbitrary ambient complete inputs. For constructible K the existing directImage_roos gives a prescribed Roos presentation L. C.push_reduction writes the actual ordinary push/reduction map as scalar extension of an isomorphism followed by an isomorphism, hence it is invertible.

At every finite level use identified-coefficient open/closed localization to obtain exactness of the canonical constant-coefficient module direct image. Its exact-derived homology comparison preserves zero cohomology. Transport across the preceding actual reduction isomorphism; this preserves every same interval including a>b. No etale-origin or bounded-complex replacement is needed.

Transport the ordinary right-derived shift through di using the fully faithful constructible inclusion and Mathlib ofComp. Compare ofComp_compatibility with the normalized ambient di shift square and cancel shifted di. Prove this calculation first for abstract full-subcategory lifts in liftedShiftInclusion, then specialize to the definition of directImageFunctor; this retains the exact object presentation in the stated inclusion equation without normalizing chosen total-limit objects. Right-derived triangulatedness restricts through the same iso. The universal-unit exact-derived comparison commutes with shifts by the existing rightExactIso_shift lemma; explicit whiskering gives closedTermwiseShift.

R.disjoint gives vanishing of the actual integral open pullback on C.pushFunctor. Transport along di.app M under integralDerivedPullback, then reflect the zero identity through the faithful constructible inclusion. This proves vanishing for the specified directImageFunctor, without changing any functor or adjunction.
